cultural.vision_reason: This is an elaborate Kalabari-style headdress (associated with Kalabari masquerade traditions like the "owu" or similar festival headgear), constructed of cardboard, wood, mirrors, feather dusters and ribbon, matching the museum's attribution "Made by: Kalabari." It is a garment/headwear made and worn by the claimed people.

physical.title: head-dress
physical.summary: Head-dress; made of cardboard and wood; hat made of cardboard, with wooden plank mounted across top; on one end "claw" shape made of four pieces of wood, decorated with glass mirrors; two curls and bird (painted white) at opposite end; at centre two tall curls and several human figures in boats; decorated with multicoloured feather dusters and red, pink, yellow and orange ribbon; textile strips hang down from either end; straps attached to cardboard for fastening head-dress.

physical.title: head-dress
physical.summary: Head-dress; made of cardboard and wood; hat made of cardboard with blue textile band around front and red, yellow and green plastic strips hanging down back; bird carved of wood on top of hat, wings outstretched, painted red with black markings, paper eye glued on, multicoloured feathers glued on top of head; cloth strips hang down from hat for tying on hat.
